meta.disclaimer: Border fees, visa rules, and insurance requirements change without notice. Figures are indicative planning estimates in our own words — always confirm with official immigration, rental companies, and insurers before travel.
meta.sourceLabel: Official immigration & COMESA sources (see each guide)

guides.title: KAZA UniVisa (Zambia & Zimbabwe)
guides.summary: One USD 50 visa for unlimited crossings between Zambia and Zimbabwe for 30 days, plus same-day Chobe day trips via Kazungula — the essential document for Victoria Falls circuits.

facts.label: Cost
facts.value: USD 50 cash on arrival

facts.label: Validity
facts.value: 30 days · multiple entries ZM ↔ ZW

facts.label: Botswana
facts.value: Day trips only via Kazungula — no overnight stay

facts.label: Payment
facts.value: USD cash — carry exact notes; cards unreliable

sections.heading: Who qualifies
sections.body: Category B nationals from around 65 countries including the UK, EU, USA, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand. SADC passport holders are usually visa-free for short visits and do not need the UniVisa. Confirm eligibility on the official list before you rely on it.

sections.heading: Where to buy it
sections.body: Available only at designated ports — not at every border or airport.
bullets: Zambia: Kenneth Kaunda (Lusaka), Harry Mwanga Nkumbula (Livingstone), Victoria Falls border, Kazungula border
Zimbabwe: Victoria Falls Airport, Victoria Falls land border, Kazungula border, Harare Airport (official list — some third-party guides note VFA/Livingstone as the main tourist entry points)
Not a substitute for Botswana, Namibia, or Mozambique entry visas

sections.heading: Planning tips
sections.body: Buy the UniVisa on first entry to Zambia or Zimbabwe if eligible. Carry clean, recent USD notes — torn or old bills are often refused. If you overnight in Botswana, the UniVisa may no longer cover re-entry — you may need a new visa.
bullets: Classic loop: Livingstone falls → bridge crossing → Victoria Falls town → Chobe day safari → return same day
Pair with our border guides for Kazungula bridge tolls and queue timing

guides.title: COMESA Yellow Card (cross-border insurance)
guides.summary: Regional third-party motor insurance valid across COMESA member states — buy before you queue instead of purchasing cover at each border post.

facts.label: What it is
facts.value: Compulsory third-party liability cover for visiting motorists

facts.label: Member states
facts.value: 13 countries incl. Zambia, Zimbabwe, Malawi, Tanzania

facts.label: SA & Mozambique
facts.value: Obtain via B2B insurers before departure — not full COMESA members

facts.label: Without it
facts.value: Fines, delays, or refusal at COMESA borders

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: The Yellow Card satisfies minimum compulsory third-party insurance in each participating country. One certificate replaces buying separate policies at border posts — saving time and often money on multi-country loops.
bullets: Obtain from your insurer, AA, or authorised broker before leaving home or in South Africa pre-departure
Rental companies may include cross-border cover in their letter of authority — confirm in writing
Valid for the period stated on the certificate; carry the original disc or certificate

sections.heading: South Africa & Mozambique travellers
sections.body: South Africa and Mozambique are not COMESA members, but the Council of Bureaux issues Yellow Cards to motorists leaving those countries under a Business-to-Business arrangement. Namibia can also issue cards for travel into COMESA territory.
bullets: Driving SA rental into Zimbabwe/Zambia/Malawi: confirm whether rental insurance or separate Yellow Card is required
Border-issued insurance is sometimes available but queues and premiums are unpredictable

guides.title: Letter of authority & rental cross-border permits
guides.summary: The document most self-drivers forget — without it, financed or rental vehicles are turned back at the border.

facts.label: Required when
facts.value: Rental, leased, or financed vehicle leaving its home country

facts.label: Typical rental fee
facts.value: Approx. ZAR 1,000–1,500 per border (arrange before pickup)

facts.label: Owned outright
facts.value: Original registration in your name + ZA sticker if SA-registered

facts.label: Lead time
facts.value: Request 5–7 days before collection — not at the counter

sections.heading: What the letter must state
sections.body: The rental company or bank issues written permission naming all countries and dates. Border officials match this to your passport and vehicle papers.
bullets: Countries permitted (list every border you plan to cross)
Vehicle registration and VIN matching the car
Named drivers on the rental agreement
Certified copy of vehicle registration if requested
Third-party insurance valid for destination — may be separate from the letter

sections.heading: Owned vehicles
sections.body: If the car is fully paid and registered in your name, you typically need the original registration certificate, proof of insurance, and a country sticker (ZA for South Africa). Financed vehicles still need bank consent.

guides.title: Driving licence & International Driving Permit
guides.summary: Left-hand traffic throughout the region. English photo licences usually accepted; Botswana strongly expects an IDP for foreign drivers.

facts.label: Traffic side
facts.value: Left-hand drive everywhere in our 9 countries

facts.label: IDP for Botswana
facts.value: Recommended for all foreign visitors

facts.label: Non-English licence
facts.value: IDP required in SA and Namibia

facts.label: Carry both
facts.value: Original home licence + IDP — never one alone

sections.heading: Country notes
sections.body: Police and rental desks may ask for an IDP even when law allows a English licence — having one avoids disputes.
bullets: South Africa: 30 days passport validity beyond departure for many visitors; licence in English or IDP
Namibia: English photo licence usually OK; IDP if not in English
Botswana: IDP recommended for all foreign drivers — rental contracts often require it
Zimbabwe & Zambia: English licences widely accepted; carry IDP as backup

guides.title: Cash, cards & border payments
guides.summary: Border posts and visa desks often cash-only. USD clean notes are the regional lingua franca for tourist fees.

facts.label: USD notes
facts.value: Clean, post-2009 series — small denominations help

facts.label: Zimbabwe
facts.value: USD widely used for tourism; ZiG for local trade

facts.label: Cards at borders
facts.value: Unreliable — assume cash for visas and road fees

facts.label: ATMs
facts.value: Major towns only — fill up before remote crossings

sections.heading: What to budget in cash
sections.body: Per-vehicle road access, carbon tax, and third-party insurance vary by country. Rental cross-border fees are paid to the company, not at the post.
bullets: KAZA UniVisa: USD 50 exact per eligible traveller
Namibia VOA/e-visa: NAD cash at some posts — confirm current N$ amount before travel
Bridge tolls: Kazungula, Beitbridge — small USD or local notes
Keep receipt stubs — some countries require exit proof of entry payment

guides.title: Night driving & road safety
guides.summary: Avoid driving after dark outside major cities — wildlife, pedestrians, and unmarked hazards cause most self-drive incidents.

facts.label: Golden rule
facts.value: Plan to reach camp by sunset

facts.label: Wildlife
facts.value: Kudu and antelope on tar — fatal at speed

facts.label: Phone use
facts.value: Illegal handheld use in South Africa

facts.label: Tyres & fuel
facts.value: Two spares for Namibia gravel; never pass last fuel stop

sections.heading: Regional hazards
sections.body: Distances between towns are long. Fuel shortages can affect Zimbabwe and Malawi — carry extra jerry cans only where legal and safe.
bullets: Namibia & Botswana: gravel punctures common — reduce speed, avoid night travel
Mozambique: police checkpoints — keep documents accessible; drive daylight hours
Lesotho: Sani Pass and high passes — weather closes routes in winter
South Africa: load shedding mostly suspended nationally in 2026, but localised load reduction still affects some townships — lodges often have backup power

borderFees.name: South Africa
borderFees.vehicleEstimate: Included in exit — ensure rental letter covers return
borderFees.notes: Unabridged birth certificate for travelling minors. ZA sticker on foreign-registered vehicles entering SA.

borderFees.name: Namibia
borderFees.notes: Cross-border fee + third-party insurance at border. Temporary import permit stamped in passport.

borderFees.name: Botswana
borderFees.notes: Third-party insurance required — Yellow Card or purchase at border. National road safety levy may apply.

borderFees.name: Zambia
borderFees.notes: COMESA Yellow Card or border insurance. KAZA UniVisa is per person, not per vehicle.

borderFees.name: Zimbabwe
borderFees.notes: Third-party insurance at border common. Carbon tax and access fees in USD.

borderFees.name: Mozambique
borderFees.notes: Third-party insurance mandatory. Yellow Card via B2B if entering from SA.

borderFees.name: Malawi
borderFees.notes: COMESA Yellow Card accepted. Fuel availability can be limited — plan ahead.
